issues.description: The problem statement and reference solution expect a function named build_msd_circ(circ: stim.Circuit, distilled_state: int, y_states: list[int]) -> tuple[list[int], list[int]], but the template repository defines a stub named build_msd_circuit(...) (with 'circuit' spelled out). This name mismatch is structural: students following the template will implement or run tests against build_msd_circuit while the tests and problem text expect build_msd_circ. This prevents straightforward completion and will cause failures or confusion when running the provided tests or comparing to the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template stub from build_msd_circuit to build_msd_circ (keeping the same signature), or provide a small wrapper in the template that defines build_msd_circ delegating to build_msd_circuit. Ensure the function name matches the problem statement and the reference solution so students and tests reference the same symbol.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution use the function name build_msd_circ(...) for constructing the distillation circuit, while the template defines build_msd_circuit(...). This naming mismatch refers to the same conceptual function (building the 15-to-1 MSD circuit) but uses two different identifiers across artifacts, which will confuse students and break a direct mapping from the problem requirements/tests to the template implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function build_msd_circuit(...) to build_msd_circ(...) so the template matches the problem statement and solution (or alternatively update the problem statement/tests and solution to use build_msd_circuit). Ensure the function signature remains the same.
